Hi Priya / Alex — Dev from Redwood here (SE) — thanks for looping me in. A few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so we can be efficient:

PrivateLink vs VPC peering (brief):
- AWS PrivateLink: Pros: cross-account connectivity, no route table changes in customer VPC, supports interface endpoints -> good for customers who prohibit peering. Cons: requires creating and accepting interface endpoints and may have per-interface costs. Latency is typically low but depends on AZ mapping.
- VPC peering: Pros: straightforward, good throughput. Cons: not transitive (if you have shared services), requires route table updates and can expose broader network surface.

Egress / IP allowlist behavior:
- Hosted API mode: outbound egress will come from Redwood-managed IP ranges (we can provide a stable list for allowlisting). Not recommended if you need isolation of compute.
- Dedicated capacity: we can provide dedicated instances with static egress IPs; better for predictable allowlists but still goes over our managed infra.
- Private VPC (preferred by Acme): traffic runs over PrivateLink or VPC peering directly into your VPC / private network; egress IP behavior depends on whether the model runtime needs to call external services. For purely inbound request/response with no external calls, egress is limited.

Required artifacts for the call:
- Your VPC CIDR ranges and preferred subnets/AZs for interface endpoints (if PrivateLink).
- If you require static egress IPs, confirm whether you can provision NAT/IP ranges in your VPC or need Redwood to supply static egress IPs.
- Point person for firewall/ACL config (Priya?)

I've attached a short network checklist and a sample CloudFormation snippet that creates the interface endpoint (will share in Drive).
